clue.text: Ground radar screens five in a thousand to find nocturnal creature

indicators.note: ground in the sense of crushed or milled, so the letters of the word beside it are broken up and reformed
to screen something is to shelter it behind you, so one piece goes around another
the whole group sits inside the outer pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for five
K is short for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A wildlife spotter uses radar to pick out a night animal somewhere among a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: RADAR is rearranged as ARD-AR with V tucked between, and that sits inside A ... K, the 'a thousand' split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal that feeds on termites after dark, so it is a creature of the night.

clue.text: A rare laborious result is a rare sight

indicators.note: the words before it are treated as raw material whose outcome is a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these three words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Something that takes painstaking effort to produce turns out to be an unusual thing to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rare' appears twice: the first is fodder, the second begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are seen only at high latitudes under the right solar conditions, so for most people they are an uncommon spectacle.

clue.text: Start off somewhere in Norfolk seen developing traffic awareness

indicators.note: the beginning is taken off, so the first letter of the place is dropped
something developing changes shape, so the letters of the neighbouring word take a new order

blocks.note: the Broads is a network of rivers and lakes in Norfolk, an English county
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something seen beginning to take shape in a Norfolk location.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is the instinct for staying safe among vehicles, which is exactly an awareness of traffic.

clue.text: Criminal's not in the building

indicators.note: says the two letters spelling that little word are absent from the criminal

blocks.note: a villain is a criminal

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is out of the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal's not in' reads as a police report; take IN out of VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a kind of house, especially a large country or holiday residence, so it is a building.

clue.text: No judge supported by America? End of trial!

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is supported sits on top, so the judge comes above the country
asks for only the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a referee judges a game
the United States of America
the last letter of trial

explanation.surface: A courtroom outburst: no judge is backed by the US, so the trial is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is giving a refusal; the single word stands for the act of declining.

clue.text: Please spread out

indicators.note: spreading things around scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread out' reads as one phrasal verb, a polite instruction; it must be split, with 'out' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out like a light is sleeping, so 'out' is a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Right after battle, sleep with someone offering wine

indicators.note: places the single letter behind the other pieces rather than in front

blocks.note: the Somme was a First World War battle
to lie down to rest
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A soldier, right after the fighting, beds down with someone who hands round drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the wine waiter in a restaurant who recommends and serves the wine.

clue.text: Crazy journey! I say you are to go and have fun

indicators.note: points to what the next words sound like when spoken, as text-speak letters
those letters are to leave the word they belong to
something crazy is disordered, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters U and R say these two words

explanation.surface: An excited traveller exclaims about a wild trip and urges a friend to go and enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U and R from JOURNEY to leave JONEY, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy oneself is to have a good time, so the verb matches having fun.

clue.text: Some make a mistake starting to excavate garden feature

indicators.note: asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: some of something is part of it
to err is to go wrong
the first letter of excavate

explanation.surface: A gardener slips up when starting to dig out part of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental flower garden laid out in patterned beds, a classic feature of grand gardens.

clue.text: Everything I entered in free form isn't fiction

definitions.note: describes the noun phrase as what is not fiction

indicators.note: something that has entered is inside, so these pieces go within the other
the letters are given a new form, a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: all is everything
taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer insists that everything they put into their free-form writing is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Real life is the actual world as opposed to invented stories, the opposite of fiction.

clue.text: An officer's scale

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a major is an army officer

explanation.surface: A military officer's rank or pay grade.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is a musical key and its scale, starting on the note A.

clue.text: Giant Marvel comic could be used in a fish & chip shop

definitions.text: could be used in a fish & chip shop

indicators.note: comic suggests something absurd and topsy-turvy, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge superhero comic book might be found on the counter of a chippy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marvel comic' reads as the publisher of superhero comics, but 'comic' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt vinegar is the brown condiment sprinkled over fried fish and chips in British takeaway shops.

clue.text: For a start, keep faith

indicators.note: the opening words keep the answer held inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of For, all of a, and the start of start

explanation.surface: Advice to begin by holding on to one's beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasta is the short name for Rastafari, the religious movement that began in 1930s Jamaica.

clue.text: Extra pounds do no harm to old city

blocks.note: to spare someone is to leave them unharmed
Tyre is an ancient Phoenician city

explanation.surface: A plea for clemency towards an ancient city, oddly linked to extra money.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is slang for a roll of fat round the waist, the visible sign of weight gained.

clue.text: Lead to centre of Greek and Latin translation

indicators.note: asks for only the middle letter of the word that follows
a translation renders a word in a different form, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: the middle letter of Greek
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Studying Greek and Latin translation leads to the heart of classical scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to bring it about as a necessary consequence, which is to lead to it.

clue.text: Save for this diary, any author's intro should be edited

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter is wanted
editing reworks text, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of author

explanation.surface: An editor tells an author to keep everything in this diary except the opening, which needs revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save for' looks like 'except', but it is the definition's verb: you save for a rainy day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'save for a rainy day' means putting money aside for hard times, so the answer completes the phrase.

clue.text: Heart hospital admitted it's not so clever

indicators.note: someone admitted to a place is let inside it, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: ticker is slang for the heart
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A cardiac hospital took in a patient, and the patient is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in after the first letter of TICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick is informal for stupid, so thicker is the comparative: less intelligent.

clue.text: What retailer does is freeze

blocks.note: first reading: a shopkeeper keeps a till, the cash register
second meaning: to stay motionless

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs the phrase re-split as KEEPS TILL, a pun on the cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop moving entirely, which is to remain motionless.

clue.text: See 1
Loves to eat free range plant

indicators.note: the letters are set free from their order and rearranged
something eating takes another thing inside it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so two loves give two Os
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sweethearts like to eat free-range food, then a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free range' looks like a farming phrase, but 'free' is the anagram signal for range.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb of the mint family, a plant used to flavour Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: Love to hear boyfriend's instrument

indicators.note: asks for a word as it sounds when spoken rather than its spelling

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a beau is a boyfriend, and the spelling here matches the sound

explanation.surface: Someone longs to listen to their partner play.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Eddy or Teddy's heading in to cause annoyance

indicators.note: a heading is at the top, so only the first letter of the name is wanted
places the short pieces inside the longer one

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Teddy
to vex is to annoy

explanation.surface: Two similar-sounding boys' names, Eddy or Teddy, getting in the way and irritating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a name paired with Teddy, but it is the definition: a whirl of water or air.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular current in water or air, a small whirlpool or vortex.

clue.text: See 11
Not allowed to listen to the Sex Pistols?

indicators.note: points to how a word is heard rather than how it is spelt

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is also true: the Sex Pistols' 'God Save the Queen' was banned by the BBC in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banned is prohibited, the formal equivalent of not permitted.

clue.text: Musician left in school toilet

indicators.note: puts the single letter inside the name of the school

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Eton is a famous English public school
john is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A musician has been left behind in a school lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton John is the British singer, songwriter and pianist behind hits such as 'Rocket Man'.

clue.text: Reject rising King Edward?

blocks.note: to rebut is to reject an argument

explanation.surface: A monarch is turned away as he attempts a rise to power.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a tuber, the swollen underground stem of the plant, so a King Edward is one.

clue.text: Some attraction in Los Angeles after setback

explanation.definitionFit: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density, so it measures some amount of magnetic attraction.

clue.text: Best map a gem

blocks.note: top means best

clue.text: Look about the same desire

explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive, a form of desire.

clue.text: For one in trouble, pity an African

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'an' looks like part of the definition 'an African', but its letters are needed in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is in north-east Africa, so an Egyptian is an African.

clue.text: Drifts and splatters?

blocks.note: first meaning: wanders off course

explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander away from a path, so strays matches drifts as a verb.

clue.text: Did this in 15: difficult riddle about puzzle centre

the two middle letters of puzzle
